why: The revocation check must be pinned to the credential the pilot ACTUALLY used. Verifying some other token would prove nothing about the exposed one, so this identity is committed here rather than supplied at dispatch time — a dispatcher cannot choose what the check is allowed to pass.
fingerprint_construction: sha256('tb4-credfp:' || token) | cut -c1-16 — the same one-way construction run-task4.sh records; never reversible to material
derived_from: all 20 runs-pilot/*-provenance.json on branch round4-pilot-state; every one records this identical fingerprint
exposure: live inside a tamper-focused agent's environment for those 20 trajectories (see DEVIATIONS, 'Credential isolation — the authoritative record', points 2-3)
cli_version_source: PILOT-EXECUTION-MANIFEST.json environment_recorded.claude_cli — read from the freeze, not duplicated here
